title: Per-tenant column mapper and pseudonymization layer for scheduled exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Why: Some enterprise customers require custom CSV column layouts, strict PII handling, and per-tenant pseudonymization rules when we deliver scheduled exports (S3 or webhook). Current export pipeline emits a fixed canonical schema and handles redaction by row-level scrubbing which creates customer support work and prevents easy downstream joinability for customers that want stable opaque IDs.

What: Implement a configurable per-tenant "column mapper" stage and an optional pseudonymization layer that replaces customer identifiers with reversible or irreversible opaque IDs based on tenant policy. The mapper will: (1) re-order and rename columns to tenant-provided templates; (2) drop or replace columns flagged as sensitive; (3) optionally emit a mapping manifest alongside the export that documents transformations (no raw PII included). The pseudonymization layer will support: reversible tokenization (tenant-managed KMS key) and irreversible hashing (salted HMAC) with tenant-configurable rotation windows.

Scope: Back-end pipeline work (export transformer service), migration of existing scheduled S3 and webhook exporters to call the transformer, small console UI hook for tenant upload of CSV templates (handed to PM/design separately), storage of per-tenant export policies in config store, and end-to-end tests including performance benchmarks for large tenants.

Out of scope: Full UI for template editing (handled in separate DES/PM ticket), audit log retention policies longer than 90 days, and transformation of binary attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant templates can be uploaded as JSON mapping and referenced by export schedules
Export pipeline applies mapping to CSVs and produces column-ordered files matching tenant template for >95% of sample cases
Pseudonymization options: reversible (KMS-wrapped token) and irreversible (HMAC) are selectable per tenant
Generated mapping manifest accompanies each export and contains no raw PII
End-to-end export latency increase <= 15% for typical 10k-row jobs and CPU/mem overhead within allocated worker limits
Automated tests cover schema mapping, missing columns, extra columns, and pseudonymization edge cases
Docs and runbook updated; security sign-off received when reversible tokens are enabled
design_notes: Transformer service will be implemented as a small Rust microservice with streaming CSV parsing to limit memory for large payloads
Template schema: list of output columns with source paths and optional transform functions (truncate, format_date, hash_column)
Reversible tokens: use tenant KMS key to encrypt an internal UUID; store token format version in manifest to support rotation
Irreversible hash: HMAC-SHA256 with tenant salt stored in config store, include salt-version metadata in manifest
For webhook exports, include a small 'transform-checksum' HTTP header so receivers can verify content integrity without revealing PII
Fallback: if tenant template references a missing field, fallback to canonical column ordering and include a warning in manifest
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal test tenant and 2 small customers, scheduled exports only (S3), monitor metrics for 48h
Phase 2: enable webhook exports and reversible tokens behind feature flag for enterprise customers with signed security review
Phase 3: open enrollment and UI hooks; default to irreversible HMAC for new tenants unless KMS key supplied
Rollback: revert to canonical exporter and mark recent exports with 'rolled_back' manifest flag
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: transform_duration_p50/p95/p99 by tenant and export size
Metric: transform_errors_total with tags (missing_field, transform_failure, kms_error)
Alert: increase in transform_errors_total > 1% for a tenant over 1h
Alert: sustained p95 transform duration > 10s for exports > 100k rows
Dashboard: per-tenant export throughput and manifest audit log sampling
